q: Which Canberra District estate co-fermented Australia's first influential Shiraz-Viognier, in 1992, and who made it?
ans: Clonakilla, by Tim Kirk — his father John Kirk had planted the vineyard at Murrumbateman in 1971
exp: Kirk took the idea from Côte-Rôtie: a small percentage of Viognier co-fermented with the Shiraz, which co-pigments to stabilise colour and lifts the aromatics. It launched a national style and, more importantly, put the Canberra District on the map — high (around 600 m) and sharply continental despite sitting at 35 degrees south.

q: Which McLaren Vale district, on deep sand over clay and ironstone, gives the region's most perfumed old-vine Grenache?
ans: Blewitt Springs — deep Maslin sands in the cooler, higher north-eastern corner of the vale
exp: Sand gives lighter colour and finer tannin, so Blewitt Springs Grenache reads high-toned and red-fruited where the heavier ironstone and clay sites toward Seaview build weight. McLaren Vale's geology map identifies some nineteen distinct geologies across a small region, and it is that map, not the GI line, that the Scarce Earth single-site Shiraz project is built on.

q: Australia's benchmark botrytis Semillon, first made in 1982, is whose wine, and from which region?
accept: de bortoli noble one from the riverina
de bortoli in new south wales
ans: De Bortoli 'Noble One', from the Riverina in inland New South Wales
exp: An irrigated bulk region produced a world-class sweet wine: autumn humidity in the Murrumbidgee irrigation area makes botrytis far more reliable than the morning fogs Sauternes depends on, so vintage variation is small. Worth holding onto as the counter-example whenever someone equates warm inland Australia with volume alone.

q: Which of these is a registered subregion of Western Australia's Great Southern GI?
exp: Great Southern's five registered subregions are Albany, Denmark, Frankland River, Mount Barker and Porongurup — the only region in Australia with that many. The other three are Margaret River districts: printed on labels, understood by the trade, but never registered, so Margaret River has no legal subregions at all.

q: Australian winemakers traditionally measure must sugar in:
exp: One degree Baumé approximates one per cent potential alcohol, so fruit picked at 14 Bé is expected to make a 14 per cent wine — roughly 1.8 Brix to the Baumé. Oechsle is German, KMW Austrian, Brix American; hearing 'we picked at 13.5' in an Australian cellar means Baumé, not alcohol already in the glass.

q: The world's oldest surviving Pinot Meunier vines (1868) and a 19th-century 'Nursery Block' of still-unidentified varieties grow at:
exp: Henry Best planted the Concongella vineyard in the 1860s and its Nursery Block still contains vines DNA testing has never fully resolved. The distractors are real old-vine claims rather than inventions: Tahbilk's is 1860 Shiraz and 1927 Marsanne, Yeringberg dates from 1863, and Seppeltsfield's treasure is the unbroken Para tawny solera begun in 1878.

q: Smaragd, Federspiel and Steinfeder are ranked by what measurement?
exp: Vinea Wachau's codex; the Wachau itself became a DAC with the 2020 vintage. Names mean feather-grass, falconry lure, emerald lizard.

q: Austria's DAC count has grown to cover most regions. What does a regional name WITHOUT DAC status imply on a label?
accept: non-typical variety sold under state name
falls back to the state designation
ans: Wines outside the DAC's typical varieties/styles label under the broader state (e.g., Niederösterreich)
exp: DAC ties region to typicity; everything else steps down a level.

q: Name the three-tier structure most DACs share.
exp: 'Ried' before a vineyard name legally marks a single site.

q: Which Kamptal Ried, a terraced Permian desert-sandstone massif, anchors Bründlmayer and Hirsch?
exp: Desert-era sandstone-volcanic conglomerate — geologically unlike anything around it.

q: The FX Pichler, Knoll and Alzinger estates cluster in which Wachau villages?
exp: Rieds Loibenberg, Schütt, Kellerberg define the eastern Wachau.

q: Ausbruch's minimum must weight places it between which two Prädikat levels?
exp: Ausbruch = BA-to-TBA botrytis tradition of Rust on the Neusiedlersee; now Ruster Ausbruch DAC.

q: Which lake's shallow warmth breeds Burgenland botrytis and ripens Zweigelt on its gravel east bank (Seewinkel)?
exp: Kracher's TBAs from Illmitz made the shore famous.

q: Beyond Mittelburgenland and Eisenberg, which Burgenland DAC is classic for Blaufränkisch?
exp: Moric's old vines re-argued the grape as 'the Pinot of the East'.

q: Gemischter Satz, protected as Wiener Gemischter Satz DAC, means:
ans: A co-planted, co-harvested, co-fermented field blend (≥3 varieties)
exp: Vienna's heurigen tradition, now fine wine (Wieninger's Nussberg).

q: Sauvignon Blanc's Austrian stronghold, with its own site classification and steep Opok marl slopes, is:
exp: 'Morillon' is local Chardonnay; the 2018 DACs brought Rieden discipline.
